fact_json.condition: host swap, hibernation, and crash capture settings
fact_json.control: review swap, hibernation, and crash-dump settings on the host
fact_json.holds: request bodies while a request runs
fact_json.how_long: during execution; host swap, hibernation, and crash-dump lifetimes depend on the machine
fact_json.reach: the machine owner and anyone with access to its files or memory image

fact_json.condition: a permitted crash dump handled by systemd-coredump
fact_json.control: review Storage and ProcessSizeMax in systemd-coredump and host core limits
fact_json.holds: a process-memory image that may contain request content
fact_json.how_long: according to the host's separate dump and journal cleanup settings
fact_json.reach: people who can read the host's crash dumps or journal
fact_json.where: systemd crash dump file and journal entry

fact_json.condition: store_prompts_in_spend_logs or its environment override is enabled
fact_json.control: inspect effective UI, environment and file settings; disable content storage and delete old rows separately
fact_json.holds: request and response content if spend-content storage is enabled
fact_json.how_long: unknown; cleanup requires a separately configured retention period
fact_json.reach: LiteLLM administrators and anyone with access to its spend database

fact_json.condition: error logging is enabled; whether a given error echoes content depends on the failure
fact_json.control: inspect disable_error_logs and effective diagnostic logging; check downstream collectors
fact_json.holds: errors and metadata that may include request content
fact_json.reach: LiteLLM administrators and downstream log readers
fact_json.where: LiteLLM error rows and downstream logs

fact_json.condition: success, failure, general or service callbacks are configured
fact_json.control: inspect effective callback settings and message omission at each destination
fact_json.holds: inputs and outputs sent to configured callbacks
fact_json.how_long: unknown; each destination has its own retention
fact_json.reach: people authorized at each configured callback destination

fact_json.condition: a LiteLLM or router cache is enabled
fact_json.control: inspect both LiteLLM and router cache settings and remove existing cache entries separately
fact_json.holds: requests and responses used for response reuse
fact_json.how_long: unknown; depends on the selected cache backend and its TTL
fact_json.reach: people authorized to read the selected cache backend
fact_json.where: LiteLLM exact or semantic cache backend

fact_json.condition: Lens ingestion or tracing integration is enabled
fact_json.control: inspect Lens ingestion and access settings independently from spend logging
fact_json.reach: administrators and viewers of all traces; other permitted users may read their own or team traces

fact_json.condition: LiteLLM has a database; counters keep virtual-key budgets working while the pinned launcher suppresses unused tool discovery
fact_json.control: use the pinned no-content launcher and inspect accounting metadata; purge old accounting with the owner's database tools only after deciding how budgets should reset
fact_json.holds: numeric key, user and team spend counters and aggregate cost and usage metadata
fact_json.how_long: according to the owner's accounting database policy; the no-content profile does not expire aggregate counters
fact_json.reach: LiteLLM administrators and anyone with access to its database
fact_json.where: LiteLLM's accounting tables; not spend rows, error rows, ToolTable or spend index rows
